subject: Follow-up: Competitor sanity checks + probe prompts from today's demo
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Adam Greene <adam@clearsky.ai>, Bethany Kim <bethany@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22 09:12 -0800
Subject: Recap + next tests from this morning's demo

Hi Adam / Bethany —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone's aligned: 

1) Recap of asks from your team
- Quality comparison vs CloudScale API for our 512-token billing scenario (few-shot instructions)
- Hallucination checks on knowledge-cutoff questions and fresh domain facts
- Latency tail (p95/p99) for concurrent bursts (10-20 rps) and expected cost per 1k tokens

2) What we committed to send today
- A lightweight evaluation matrix (attached: eval_matrix_v1.xlsx) that lists the prompt families, metrics (EM, F1 where applicable), hallucination check design, and suggested labeling rules.
- A probe prompt pack (attached: probe_prompts_v2.txt) containing ~40 targeted prompts to reproduce the edge hallucinations you flagged.
- Raw latency samples from the demo run we mentioned (attached: latency_samples_11-22.csv).

3) Proposed next tests (please confirm priority):
- Run our probe pack vs CloudScale and ClearSky baseline with identical few-shot context (3 examples) and report hallucination flags + confidence scores. Target: overnight run.
- A short A/B for prompt engineering: our default system prompt vs your current system prompt to measure behavioral delta.
- A tail-latency stress test: 20 concurrent clients for 15 minutes to reproduce p99 spikes.

4) Logistics & handoffs
- If you want Redwood to run these tests on your behalf, we can spin up a short Dedicated evaluation pool (24h) for reproducibility. Rough estimate: $X/day (we'll formalize if you want).
- Otherwise we'll provide the scripts and baseline outputs so your infra team can run them.

Please reply with: (A) which tests you want Redwood to execute, and (B) whether we should include cost-normalized throughput numbers in the report.

Thanks — I can start the runs as soon as I get a go-ahead.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | inference@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
From: Adam Greene <adam@clearsky.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22 10:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next tests from this morning's demo

Thanks Jasmine — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Please run the probe pack vs CloudScale and Redwood. We don't need ClearSky to run anything; we'd like an apples-to-apples output to review.
- Prioritize hallucination checks and the 20-client tail-latency stress test. Quality metrics second (EM/F1 where applicable).
- For cost normalization: yes, please include cost per 1k tokens and cost per successful response (we'll need that to compare tradeoffs).

If possible, tag any runs where you used quantized model variants vs full-precision. We suspect CloudScale is using an aggressively quantized path that may explain some noise.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Adam
Adam Greene
Head of Engineering, ClearSky AI
adam@clearsky.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Adam Greene <adam@clearsky.ai>, Bethany Kim <bethany@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22 12:15 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next tests from this morning's demo

Looping in a couple of quick implementation notes before we start the runs: 

- We'll run the probe pack with identical few-shot context and temperature settings (T=0.2 and T=0.7) to capture stochasticity. Outputs will include model logits when available.
- For the tail-latency stress test we'll run both our hosted API (to match what you saw) and a short-lived Dedicated pool using A100s so the p99 comparison is fair.
- We'll tag runs in the eval_matrix with the model variant (e.g., redwood-helix-q4_1, redwood-helix-fp16) and include a small README in the Drive link describing run configs.

Jasmine — we'll need the final priority list from Adam, and confirmation if ClearSky wants the runs completed by tomorrow EOD or if next-week is OK.

Rishi
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Bethany Kim <bethany@cloudscale.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Adam Greene <adam@clearsky.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22 16:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next tests from this morning's demo

Hey all — thanks for pulling this together. Quick confirmation from CloudScale:

- We approve Redwood running the same probe pack on your infra for apples-to-apples. Please include the quantized flags as Rishi noted.
- Priority order: (1) hallucination probe results, (2) tail-latency stress test, (3) cost-normalized throughput.
- Aim for preliminary results by EOD tomorrow (11/23). If that's too tight, early next week is acceptable but we prefer faster.

Also, one ask from our side: please add a short human-reviewed sample set (10 responses) for each model-run so we can sanity-check automated hallucination flags. That will help avoid false positives.

Thanks — Bethany
Bethany Kim
Product Manager, CloudScale
attachments referenced: eval_matrix_v1.xlsx; probe_prompts_v2.txt; latency_samples_11-22.csv
